stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab: Andhra Pradesh puts estimated loss at ₹4,600 crore
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab: Andhra Pradesh puts estimated loss at ₹4,600 crore
stories.summary: Central team to arrive in Andhra Pradesh to assess cyclone damage October 30; A.P. urges Telangana to deploy 1,000 personnel for power restoration work in the Godavari region
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh has suffered an estimated loss of ₹4,600 crore due to Cyclone Arnab as per the preliminary assessment, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said on Thursday.
Mr. Naidu made an aerial survey of cyclone-hit areas in the Krishna and Godavari regions.
He inspected the areas on the way to Cheyyeru village in Katrenikona mandal of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district.

After interacting with flood victims at Gacchakayala Pora village of Mummidivaram mandal, Mr. Naidu told the media that the cyclone preparedness helped check the loss of lives as the casualty was seven.
He said the Telangana government had been urged to depute 1,000 staff to ensure speedy restoration of power supply.
“If need be, we will request Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to send 2,000 more personnel to be engaged in the power restoration work, mostly in the Godavari region.

Power restoration work will be finished quickly, and the supply will resume by Saturday,” Mr. Naidu said, addign that at least 8,000 electric poles were uprooted in Dr. B.R.Ambedkar Konaseema district alone.
Mr. Naidu assured that machines would be brought from other States to ensure speedy installation of electric poles.
The Chief Minister said, “ A compensation of ₹1,500 will be given for each coconut and oil palm tree that fell under the influence of the cyclone.
The compensation and input subsidy will be decided immediately after the enumeration of the damage done to agriculture and horticulture crops,” he said.
A ₹25-kg rice bag and cash each would be given away to the families who were shifted to relief camps.
The Chief Minister also said that he had briefed Union Home Minister Amit Shah about the damage done by the Cyclone Arnab.

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh Minister tells official to expedite restoration works in cyclone-hit towns
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh Minister tells official to expedite restoration works in cyclone-hit towns
stories.summary: Of the 85 locations in 10 municipalities affected by Cyclone Arnab, normalcy has been restored in 71 locations across seven municipalities so far, say officials
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana on Thursday directed the officials to expedite restoration works and bring life back to normal in cyclone-affected areas across Andhra Pradesh.

During a teleconference with Municipal Administration Department Commissioner and Director P. Sampath Kumar, Public Health Engineering-in-Chief Prabhakar and Municipal Commissioners, the Minister reviewed the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab and the progress of relief and restoration measures.
Officials informed the Minister that 85 locations in 10 municipalities across eight districts had been affected by the cyclone.
Normalcy had been restored in 71 locations across seven municipalities so far, they said.
The officials said that fallen trees and electric poles had been cleared.
In areas where power supply remained disrupted, drinking water was being supplied using generators to ensure that residents did not face shortages.
Mr. Narayana instructed the Municipal Commissioners to prioritise sanitation and maintain cleanliness in affected localities to prevent public health problems.
He directed officials to ensure that streetlights were fully functional by Thursday evening.
The Minister stressed the need for coordinated efforts among departments to complete the restoration works swiftly.

stories.headline: Post-Arnab cyclone, heavy rain wreaks havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati districts
stories.title: Post-Arnab cyclone, heavy rain wreaks havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati districts
stories.summary: More than 200 villages in 22 blocks across Ganjam and Gajapati districts severely affected; roads washed away, villages marooned and three rivers are in spate
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Heavy rain triggered by cyclone Arnab wreaked havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts on Thursday (October 29, 2026), washing away roads, marooning villages and triggering landslides, as State officials struggled to restore normalcy.
The rainfall recorded in the three districts was among the highest ever recorded.
“Exceptionally heavy rainfall occurred over south Odisha during the past 24 hours, ending at 8.30 a.m. on Thursday.

The highest rainfall of 546 mm was recorded at Patrapur [Ganjam], followed by 503 mm at Sorada [Ganjam], 462 mm at G. Udayagiri [Kandhamal], 458 mm at Mahendragarh [Gajapati], 388 mm at Sanakhemundi [Ganjam] and 309 mm at Chikiti (Ganjam),” the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said.
A stretch of the National Highway 326 connecting Berhampur with Mohana was washed away by swirling floodwaters, disrupting road connectivity.
Road infrastructure also suffered extensive damage in Gajapati district.
The hilly terrain compounded the situation, as torrents of rainwater rushed downhill into low-lying areas, triggering landslides and damaging infrastructure.
At several places, floodwaters flowed over major roads, halting vehicular movement in the two districts.
In Ganjam district alone, 42,500 people were marooned by floodwaters, while 11,000 people were shifted from vulnerable areas to designated shelters.
With roads cut off and hundreds of villages inundated by floodwaters in Ganjam, the State government roped in the Coast Guard to airlift people stranded in Dharakote block.

“In response to a distress call received from the Ganjam district administration on the morning of October 29, 2026, the Coast Guard Air Enclave, Bhubaneswar, scrambled an ALH Mk-III helicopter despite severe weather conditions,” the Coast Guard said in a statement.
“Despite challenging conditions, the aircrew located the heavily inundated Public Health Centre in Jagmohan, where people were stranded by floodwaters following the storm.

stories.headline: Floods leave AP-Odisha border villages inundated, traffic on NH-16 disrupted
stories.title: Flash floods leave AP-Odisha border villages inundated, traffic on NH-16 disrupted
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Life has become miserable for thousands of people living in Ichchapuram and surrounding villages, including Loddaputti, Korigam, Rattakanna and others, along the Andhra Pradesh- Odisha border, after flash floods inundated low-lying areas following surge of water in the Bahuda river and seasonal streams.
The flooding followed the release of large volume of water from the Baghalati Dam located in the Patrapur block of Odisha’s Ganjam district, inundating many border villages.
Traffic on National Highway-16, which connects Chennai-Kolkata was also disrupted by the overflowing river Bahuda and seasonal streams.
Odisha irrigation officials alerted their AP counterparts before releasing around 86,000 cusecs of water from the dam on Thursday afternoon.

The Srikakulam district administration had also taken steps to relocate people, but the evacuation was done only partially as it was late at night and there was no much time to inform all the villagers.
Power outages, lack of internet connectivity, added to the residents woes.
Streets in several villages turned into flowing streams, preventing people from moving to safer places.
“People living in Ichchapuram and surrounding villages were shocked with the sudden surge of floodwater at night.
In the absence of internet connectivity on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) night residents were unable to contact any official,” said Tarunraj, an advocate from Ichchapuram.
Former Ichchapuram MLA Piriya Sairaj alleged that the government had utterly failed in taking up adequate relief measures in the flood-affected areas.

Srikakulam District Congress Committee president Sanapala Annaji Rao said that the government could have averted inundation of the villages if it had properly coordinated with the Odisha administration.
Meanwhile, the administration sent National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and special teams to the border town, which is almost 120 km from Srikakulam district headquarters.

stories.headline: Supreme Court strikes down Karnataka law validating ‘corrupt’ 2011 recruitment
stories.title: Supreme Court strikes down Karnataka law validating ‘corrupt’ 2011 recruitment
stories.summary: Top court says cancellation of the recruitment process was upheld by both HC and SC, and that the 'power does not lie with the legislature to annul the cancellation, even by a legislation, and thus nullify the judgments of the Constitutional courts’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'strikes down' in title weight 40
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) declared unconstitutional a Karnataka State law, which validated the 2011 selection of Gazetted Probationers made through what the court described as a “corrupt” and “blatantly nepotistic” recruitment process conducted by the State Public Service Commission.

A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held that the Karnataka Civil Services (Validation of Selection and Appointment of 2011 Batch Gazetted Probationers) Act, 2022, was enacted clearly with the intent to countermand the judgments of both the Karnataka High Court and the Supreme Court.
The courts had upheld the decision to cancel the entire 2011 recruitment process for 362 posts of Group ‘A’ and ‘B’ Officers.

“The cancellation having been upheld by the High Court and the Supreme Court, the power does not lie with the legislature to annul the cancellation, even by a legislation, and thus nullify the judgments of the Constitutional courts,” Justice Chandran said.
The court highlighted how the State government, represented by senior advocate Kapil Sibal, constantly changed its position over a decade “depending on the hues and colours in the changing times”.

The State had, over the years, swung between supporting the cancellation of the entire recruitment process and enacting the 2022 law, leaving the hapless candidates caught in the crosshairs of shifting political whims and systemic failure.

“When the winds of politics change direction, it is the common man who gets caught in the storm… A recruitment of 2011 is hanging fire still, putting to peril the aspirations of many… Six appellants [represented by senior advocate Shyam Divan] who would be over-aged now have relentlessly pursued their cause in their zeal to join the Karnataka Civil Services,” Justice Chandran observed.
The 2011 recruitment process saw 1,38,307 people apply.

Two years later, a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) inquiry found “gross manipulations” in the process, and “the irregularities in evaluation of answer scripts were found to be shockingly disgraceful”.
On Thursday, the Supreme Court upheld the cancellation of the entire recruitment based on a 2011 notification.
It said no equity could be granted to untainted successful candidates, represented by senior advocate Sanjay Nuli, who were selected on the strength of the 2022 Act.
The court termed the Act a “stillborn legislation”.

stories.headline: Our orders breached ‘left and right’, Deepavali was a festival of lights before gunpowder, Supreme Court says in firecrackers case
stories.title: Our orders breached ‘left and right’, Deepavali was a festival of lights before gunpowder, Supreme Court says in firecrackers case
stories.summary: A complete ban may have a ‘spiralling effect’, the court says, asks the Centre and the Delhi government to ensure enforcement against sellers of spurious and banned crackers
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said its orders, year after year, to curb and even ban firecrackers during Deepavali, had been violated “left and right”.
A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale said the right to religious freedom was also subject to public health and the protection of fundamental rights.

Justice Sundresh said the incessant bursting of firecrackers takes a toll on the health of a large section of the population, including children, the aged, the sick, pregnant women, and specially-abled persons.
Justice Sundresh reminded that Deepavali is called the ‘festival of lights’.
“The problem might have started with gun powder,” the judge said.
The court was hearing a case on the increase in pollution as the festival drew near amidst the loud bangs of firecrackers.
“We understand the sentiments of the public.
If we think in a logical sense, celebrations do boost morale,” Justice Sundresh said.
The court also empathised with officers’ hesitations to book criminal cases against ordinary people who were “enthusiastic” about celebrations.
Justice Sundresh said the court was not in favour of a complete ban.
“That may have a spiralling effect.
But having said that, please do not push us to take harsh actions,” the Bench said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court calls for financial institutions to compensate digital arrest victims
stories.title: Supreme Court calls for financial institutions to compensate digital arrest victims
stories.summary: The Bench stressed that the proposed regulatory framework must provide for suitable compensation to victims where financial institutions are found to have failed in their due diligence obligations
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Observing that banks must be made accountable to indemnify losses of victims of digital fraud, the Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said victims of offences like digital arrests should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if the fraud is found to have resulted from a failure of due diligence by the financial institution.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it would examine the Reserve Bank of India's proposed Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026, which are expected to be notified by November 30 and operationalised by December 31.
The Bench stressed that the proposed regulatory framework must provide for suitable compensation to victims where financial institutions are found to have failed in their due diligence obligations.

It also reiterated the need for mandatory preventive measures, including temporarily suspending unusual transactions that deviate from an account holder's established transaction pattern, automated reporting of suspicious activity and physical verification to establish the genuineness of transactions.
The Court further said that it is the responsibility of banks to alert neighbouring police stations about unusual transactions involving customers who may be victims of digital arrest scams.
The Bench asked the RBI to provide details of the financial institutions that would be covered by the proposed guidelines and the measures being considered to compensate victims for their losses.

During the hearing, Attorney General R. Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre and other authorities, informed the Court that reported digital arrest cases had declined by around 50% compared with the previous year, attributing the reduction to the Court's intervention, coordinated action by government ministries and departments, and public awareness campaigns.
The CJI, however, pointed out that the country had still suffered losses of nearly ₹800 crore from such offences this year.

The CJI identified two key areas requiring further intervention, the accountability of banks and the problem of mule accounts, which are frequently used to receive and transfer proceeds of cybercrime.

The matter, titled In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents, is being monitored by the Supreme Court as part of efforts to strengthen the country's institutional response to cyber-enabled financial fraud.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court Collegium has approved the proposal for appointment of nine advocates as Judges of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
The decision was taken at a Collegium meeting held on October 29, 2026, according to a statement issued by the Supreme Court Collegium.
The recommendations follow an earlier exercise by the High Court Collegium, headed by Chief Justice Arun Palli, which had recommended 11 names for appointment as High Court Judges in April this year.
The recommendations comprised 10 advocates from the Bar quota and one judicial officer from the Bench quota.
The earlier recommendations were part of an exercise to address vacancies in the High Court, whose sanctioned strength had been increased from 17 to 25 Judges in November 2024.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu Cabinet clears incentives for eight new industrial projects worth ₹3,767 crore
stories.summary: The proposed projects span emerging sectors, including technical textiles, aerospace and defence, life sciences and electronics, among others, according to sources
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Tamil Nadu Cabinet, headed by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, on Thursday approved a structured package of incentives for eight new industrial companies setting up or expanding projects across Coimbatore, Krishnagiri, Kanchipuram, Chengalpattu and Erode districts, involving investments of ₹3,767 crore and generating employment opportunities for 4,853 people.
The proposed projects span emerging sectors, including technical textiles, aerospace and defence, life sciences and electronics, among others, according to sources.
The Cabinet also approved the expansion plans of three companies.
The government did not disclose the names of the companies or provide a district-wise break-up of the investments and employment generation.
Separately, the Cabinet approved a proposal to constitute a multi-member commission, headed by a retired High Court judge, to conduct the Social Justice Survey.
Briefing the media after the Cabinet meeting, CTR Nirmal Kumar said the survey was one of the key poll promises of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) ahead of the 2026 Assembly election.
The Governor’s inaugural address to the State Assembly had also referred to the proposal.
The survey is expected to be conducted next year, after the completion of the ongoing Census.
The commission to oversee the exercise will be constituted by February or March next year, he said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Says Banks Must Compensate Cyber Fraud Victims If It Took Place Due To Bank's Lack Of Due Diligence
stories.title: Supreme Court Says Banks Must Compensate Cyber Fraud Victims If It Took Place Due To Bank's Lack Of Due Diligence
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: In the digital arrest matter, the Supreme Court today expressed that financial institutions must face strict liability in the event of a customer becoming victim to digital arrest/cyber fraud if the institution/its officials are found negligent in exercise of due diligence.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was dealing with the suo motu case taken up over rising incidents of digital arrest scams.
Yesterday, the CJI took a strong view on persons accused in such crimes, saying that if law permits, such "ruthless criminals" targeting senior citizens must be punished even before trial.

Today, the Court was told by Attorney General R Venkataramani that while many steps have been taken to address the menace, the RBI is contemplating regulatory measures, which are likely to be operationalized by December.

Considering Senior Advocate NS Nappinai's (Amicus) submission that despite the court taking cognizance of the matter and passing various directions, digital arrest incidents are rampantly taking place (last reported a week ago), the bench questioned why RBI was still consulting banks.
"Problem is - bank officials are involved.
Even when we are asking to [take steps], RBI is consulting the banks!", the CJI commented.
The CJI also questioned the AG as to why banks, which have a complete record of amounts in people's accounts, don't intervene to stop suspicious or fraudulent messages asking for money.
"They know very well who is the account holder.
The moment you know there's amount lying in account, banks must create protective umbrella.
Why don't [banks] stop messages asking for money?
The moment a transaction comes, why can't it be withheld?"

stories.headline: Gold steady at Rs 1.46 lakh/10 gm in Delhi; silver rises Rs 500/kg
stories.title: Gold steady at Rs 1.46 lakh/10 gm in Delhi; silver rises Rs 500/kg
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 29: Gold prices were steady at Rs 1.46 lakh per 10 grams in the national capital on Thursday as jewellers and retailers remained cautious about fresh purchases amid elevated rates. Silver prices, however, rose by Rs 500 to Rs 1,98,500 per kilogram, inclusive of all taxes, according to the All India Sarafa Association. The white metal closed unchanged at Rs 1.98 lakh per kg on Wednesday. Traders said gold prices remained steady as jewellers and retailers were cautious about fresh buying amid high prices. "Domestic gold prices remained steady on Thursday, following range-bound movements in international markets amid mixed signals," said Saumil Gandhi, Senior Analyst of Commodities at HDFC Securities. A hawkish stance by the US Federal Reserve overshadowed support from a decline in US Treasury yields and crude oil prices, he said. In international markets, spot gold fell by USD 49.38, or 1.21 per cent, to USD 4,018.08 per ounce, while silver declined 3 per cent to USD 52.41 per ounce. "Gold remained under pressure to hover around USD 4,024 per ounce on Thursday, as the Federal Reserve's hawkish outlook and persistent energy-driven inflation strengthen expectations of further monetary policy tightening," said Vedika Narvekar, Research Analyst- Commodities & Currencies, Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Ltd. Firm crude oil prices, uncertainty around the Fed's policy path and equity-market liquidations are adding to volatility, although geopolitical risks and central-bank buying may offer support, she said.
